=SEO Content Writing SOPs 

SOP 1 — General SEO Content Writing Process
Follow this process for every piece of content, start to finish. 

1. Pre-Writing: Research & Planning
● Primary Keyword: pick one main focus keyword
● Secondary Keywords: list 3–5 related (LSI) keywords
● Search Intent: confirm it matches informational, transactional, navigational, or commercial intent
● Word Count: standard blogs = 1,000–1,200 words; pillar/comparison = 1,500+ words
● Content Brief: outline with H1/H2/H3, pick a content angle (guide, listicle, how-to, review)
● Add AT LEAST 5 distinct FAQs from “People Also Ask” + competitor pages
● Define clear CTAs (e.g. “Contact us,” “Shop now”)

2. Writing: Title, Headings & Meta
● H1 Title: primary keyword included naturally, under 60 characters
● Current Year Rule: Always use 2026 as the current year for temporal statements, titles, or current guide recommendations. Never use past years like 2024 or 2025 unless referencing historical data.
● Use H2/H3 subheadings with secondary/LSI keywords in logical order (never skip levels)
● Meta Title: under 60 characters, includes main keyword
● Meta Description: 150–160 characters, engaging, includes primary keyword

3. Writing: Content Body
● Primary keyword MUST appear in the first 100 words of the opening paragraph
● Keyword density 1%–1.5% — natural, never stuffed
● Short sentences (15–20 words max) and short paragraphs (2–3 lines / under 100 words)
● Use bullet points, lists, and visuals to break up text
● Match or exceed target word count (1,000–1,200 words minimum)
● Content must be original, actionable, and solve the reader's problem

🔗 Linking Rules
• Internal links: 5–7 per post, place the first link in the intro paragraph, 2–3 word anchor text
• External links: Exactly 1 to a high-authority pre-approved source (DA 50+), opens in new tab, never link competitors

⚙️ 4. On-Page SEO Checks
● At least 1 image per 500 words with keyword-optimized alt text
● Optimize for featured snippets (lists, tables, Q&A format)
● Include an FAQ section with AT LEAST 5 Q&A pairs
● Short, descriptive, keyword-rich URL slug
● Natural CTA (form, button, or link)

✅ 5. Post-Writing Checklist
☑ Grammarly score 90+ (no grammar issues)
☑ 100% unique — checked with Copyscape/Quetext
☑ Readability at Grade 6–8 (Hemingway/Yoast standard)
☑ Proper heading hierarchy: H1 → H2 → H3
☑ Keywords used naturally, no stuffing
☑ Internal & external links inserted correctly
☑ Alt text added on all images
☑ Word count matches the brief (1,000–1,200+ words)

--------------------------------------------------

SOP 2 — Local SEO Blog Rules
Apply these rules on top of SOP 1 for every blog written for a local or service-area client.

1. Keyword & Topic Selection
● 1 primary keyword + 2–3 supporting local keywords
● Topic must tie to a current trend (seasonal demand, viral DIY fails, rising energy costs) or a frequently searched local problem

🏙️ 2. Local Optimization (Required on Every Post)
● Include primary city + "city, state" naturally in the title, intro, H2s, and conclusion
● Use hyper-local phrasing: “homeowners in [City],” “[City] HVAC codes,” “common [City] plumbing issues”
● Reference local landmarks, climate, or regulations where it fits naturally

3. Blog Structure
● Title — primary keyword + city + 2026 (e.g. “Best Water Heater Upgrades for [City] Homeowners in 2026”)
● Intro (100–150 words) — hook + primary keyword in first 100 words + local context
● H2 sections (3–5) — each targeting a supporting keyword or question
● FAQ Section — minimum 5 local/service FAQs
● Local CTA — ends with a call to action naming the city and service

4. Style & Consistency
● Tone: conversational but professional — no jargon, no fluff
● Length: 1,000–1,200 words for standard posts; 1,500+ for pillar posts
● No walls of text — short paragraphs, H2/H3 subheadings, plain bullet lists

=={{ "Follow this SOP exactly (word count, keyword density, internal/external linking, tone): " + $('SOP Reference1').first().json.sop_text + " Write the full blog post from this brief. Brief: " + $json.candidates[0].content.parts[0].text + " CRITICAL WORD COUNT & CONTENT RULES: - TARGET WORD COUNT: You MUST write a comprehensive, in-depth article of AT LEAST 1,000 to 1,200 words (or 1,500+ words for pillar/comparison guides). Do not write brief summaries or cut sections short. Expand thoroughly on every main point, scenario, and process step to meet this exact length target. - CURRENT YEAR: The current year is 2026. Always reference 2026 (or future dates) for any temporal statements, titles, or current recommendations. Do not use past years like 2024 or 2025 unless discussing past historical data. - INTRO PARAGRAPH & KEYWORD: You MUST place the exact primary keyword ('" + $('Loop Over Items1').first().json.selected_keyword + "') inside the first 100 words of the introductory paragraph. - FAQS SECTION: You MUST include AT LEAST 5 distinct Frequently Asked Questions with thorough, helpful answers at the end of the post under '## Frequently Asked Questions'. STRICT FORMATTING RULES: - Do not use emojis anywhere in the content. - Do not use em dashes (—) or en dashes (–). Use commas, periods, or restructure the sentence instead. - Do not use bullet points with checkmark or emoji markers — use plain markdown dashes or numbers only. - Write in a natural, human tone. Avoid phrases that sound distinctly AI-generated, such as overly formal transitions ('Furthermore,', 'In conclusion,'), excessive rhetorical questions, or repetitive sentence structures. - Base all analysis on original thinking and your own synthesis of the competitor research provided. Do not closely paraphrase or lift sentence structures from the competitor content — write in your own words and structure throughout. - Vary sentence length for natural rhythm, but NEVER exceed 20 words in any single sentence. Mix short, punchy sentences of 5 to 8 words with medium sentences of 12 to 18 words. Do not let more than two consecutive sentences fall into a similar length or rhythm. - Include at least three specific, concrete details that could not be found by summarizing the competitor pages provided. This could be a specific realistic example, a genuine process detail, a local or industry specific, or a concrete scenario. Generic, summarized advice reads as AI generated. Specific, concrete detail does not. - Avoid starting consecutive paragraphs with similar sentence structures or transition words. Do not open more than one paragraph in the piece with the same word. - Do not include any tags, image placeholders, or references to images (such as 'image1.jpg', '[image here]', or similar) anywhere in the content. Images are inserted programmatically after generation — write pure text content only, with no image markup of any kind. READABILITY RULES (follow exactly, these are graded automatically): - Use simple, everyday words over complex ones wherever possible. Write at a 6th to 8th grade reading level. - Keep every paragraph to 3 sentences or fewer, and under 100 words total. Break up any longer thought into two shorter paragraphs. - Use active voice for at least 90% of sentences. Avoid passive constructions like 'was created by' or 'is used to' - write 'we created' or 'you use' instead. - Include a genuine transition word or phrase (such as 'however', 'because', 'as a result', 'meanwhile', 'for example', 'in fact', 'that said') in at least 1 out of every 3 sentences, varied throughout and never repeated back to back. - Place an H2 or H3 subheading at least once every 250 to 300 words. Never let a section run longer than that without a subheading break. LINKING RULES (follow exactly): - Use 5 to 7 internal links total across the post, drawn from the internal link candidates provided in the brief. - Place the first internal link within the opening paragraph of the article, not later. - Every internal link's anchor text must be only 2 to 3 words long. Never link a full phrase like 'comprehensive digital marketing services' - link a short fragment like 'digital marketing' instead, with the rest of the sentence as plain text around it. - Use exactly 1 external link total, chosen ONLY from this pre-approved list, never invent or guess your own external URL: " + JSON.stringify($('Get External Link Candidates2').first().json.external_link_candidates) + ". If none of these fit the topic naturally, omit the external link entirely rather than inventing one. OUTPUT FORMAT (use real markdown syntax exactly as shown, since this gets converted to HTML automatically): META_TITLE: [under 60 characters, include 2026 if year referenced] META_DESCRIPTION: [150-160 characters] URL_SLUG: [slug here] # [The actual H1 title, as a real markdown heading. This MUST be 60 characters or fewer, counted exactly. It should closely match META_TITLE in wording and length, not just start the same way and then run longer. If your first draft of this title exceeds 60 characters, shorten it by cutting words, not by using abbreviations or removing spaces.] IMPORTANT: Respond with plain text only. Do not wrap your response in a JSON object, do not add any JSON keys or braces around it, and do not add any commentary before or after — output only the raw content exactly as specified below. [Full blog body here, in proper markdown: use ## for H2 sections, ### for H3 subsections, **text** for bold emphasis, - for bullet lists, 1. 2. 3. for numbered lists. Do not use any other heading level or label. Do not write out words like 'BODY:' or 'H1 TITLE:' as literal text — only use real markdown symbols.] ## Frequently Asked Questions [Provide AT LEAST 5 detailed Q&A pairs, each question as **bold text**] [Final CTA paragraph, no separate label, just the CTA sentence itself as the last paragraph, plain text only - do not include a hyperlink, button, or markdown link syntax here, a real CTA button will be added automatically after your content]" }}
